title: Change Mentor email practice software
summary: Change Mentor selection, reply processing, retention, grading integration, public commands or installation while preserving the small independent-answer email loop and provider authority.
use_when: The requested work changes Mentor code, corpus format, state, invocation policy, CLI, installation, provider bundle or documentation.
do_not_use_when: The request is an ordinary practice or installed administration operation.
The change would add an answer archive, ongoing tutoring, arbitrary recipients, direct Resend access or a direct-model fallback without an explicit new scope.
outcome: A minimal owning source change with synchronized product and shared contracts; validation, publication and deployment remain separate operations governed by the task authority.
effects: Modifies authorized Mentor source, data format, model policy, packaging and documentation. Shared Email/Nucleus/Clockwork changes require their selected owning interfaces and instructions.
A future deployment can change private state and scheduled operation; source editing does not install, schedule, submit a model job or send email.
authority: Mentor owns exact temporary requests, answer eligibility, corpus identity, selection, retention and accepted-submission rules.
Email owns transport and addresses; Nucleus owns runtime/authentication/retention; Clockwork owns activation. Do not copy provider wire structs or use their private databases.
success: Source, public CLI/types, corpus/state semantics, retention, provider dependencies and manuals describe the same scoped implementation.
Report which verification was performed or explicitly deferred by the task; do not present coding-only work as tested, installed or ready.
failure_and_recovery: Keep the exact frozen request and send-key invariants, pending-content expiry, body-free diagnostics and explicit unknown outcomes.
State changes require a supported migration/backup and database-aware recovery policy before deployment; never repair private rows directly.
privacy: Use authored corpus data and synthetic answers in source examples. Do not copy live inbox content, credentials, grading responses or Nucleus records into source/contracts.
does_not_authorize: Tests, builds, releases, commits, installs, live jobs, sends or configuration effects that the task forbids or has not authorized.
An automatic answer archive, zero-retention claim, provider record deletion, alternate model path or arbitrary send recipient.
steps: Read product instructions and applicable maintained terminology, using Cell until Mentor has a registered semantic repository.
Read the affected practice/installation/Email/Nucleus/Clockwork contracts; read nucleus manual for state or requester changes.
Implement the smallest owning change and synchronize product contracts plus the shared operator manual when shared facts change.
Perform only the validation and later effects permitted by the task, and report any deferred evidence.
checkpoints: No answer or critique archive; temporary content expiry and acceptance cleanup remain explicit.
Assignment/corpus identity survives late replies and content refresh without resetting used problem IDs.
Provider-owned typed clients preserve credentials, fixed addresses and exact invocation identity.
A source bundle is not presented as installed discovery or live readiness.
adaptation: Publish a new input or corpus identity when a meaning changes incompatibly; retain old corpus data needed for assignments.
Changes to provider receiving, headers, model permissions, retention or schedule meaning belong to the owning product contract as well as Mentor.
stop_when: The implementation uses a private provider database, hidden execution fallback, arbitrary sender-selected destination or undeclared archive.
The requested state or lifecycle change cannot preserve supported recovery, privacy and ownership.

consumers.statement: An authorized contributor changes the small Mentor service and its declared integration boundaries.

preconditions.statement: Read product instructions, registered Mentor terminology when available or Cell otherwise, affected installed contracts and the current Nucleus manual before requester/state/lifecycle changes.

inputs.statement: Inputs are the requested change, current owning source and contracts, authored corpus artifact and synthetic development examples.

outputs.statement: Output is synchronized source/documentation with the performed or deferred verification stated accurately. Development does not itself install, enable, send or grade.

data_semantics.statement: Preserve assignment reservation versus acceptance, provider IDs versus RFC IDs, current local-date selection, independent answers, temporary work versus retained metadata and provider retention boundaries.

identity_and_units.statement: Keep stable problem IDs, frozen corpus digests, immutable Nucleus request IDs, exact send keys, byte bounds and explicit timestamp units. Incompatible meaning changes require new versioned identity.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: The change description must identify affected interfaces and evidence actually obtained. Source publication alone makes no claim about installed dependency availability.
No implementation duration, validation success, deployment readiness or future support lifetime is promised before its separate evidence exists.

access.statement: Use provider-owned typed clients and supported commands. No private Email/Nucleus/Clockwork database edits, credential copying, direct-Codex or direct-Resend fallback.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: State changes require supported migration, drained content-free backup and compatible rollback semantics. Source and matching provider contract changes stay together; actual installation and activation remain separate effects.

operational_limits.statement: Keep one small product runner and the defined input/output/expiry limits. Do not broaden into a history service, workflow engine or generic email platform.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Private state, corpus, grading input, provider contracts and installed release have separate versions. Preserve source compatibility at Email boundaries and exact historical assignment interpretation.

reliances.statement: Semantics supplies maintained terms; Cell is the explicit fallback until Mentor is registered.
Nucleus integration defines closed invocation and requester-owned success/recovery.
